stem:
Reyansh plans his family's school-week travel to cut petrol and diesel use. Nearby trips can be walked or cycled; longer trips can use a shared bus; a private car burns petrol for every short hop. They also discuss idle engine time while waiting.

Answer both parts.

parts.text: Which claim correctly reduces fossil-fuel use?

options.text: Walk or cycle for nearby trips and share a bus for longer ones so less petrol and diesel are burned.
Drive the private car for every nearby trip so the bus is never needed.
Always pick the smallest car, because the smallest vehicle must use the least petrol on every trip.
Keep the car engine idling while waiting, because an idling engine uses no petrol.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Walking, cycling, and shared buses cut petrol and diesel use. More private-car trips, judging only by car size, or assuming idle engines use no fuel do not reduce fossil-fuel use.

teacher.key_rationale: Walking, cycling, and shared public transport reduce fossil-fuel use; extra car trips, size alone, and idle-engine myths miss the hinge.
